rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says that supplication is worship.
rows.anchor: في الحديث: «الدعاء العبادة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplication may be the prayer Abraham recited in al-Shuʿaraʾ, asking for wisdom and joining the righteous.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الدعاء الذي حكاه الله في سورة الشعراء رب هب لي حكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham contrasts the unbelievers' invocation of their gods with his humble hope in his Lord; the word ʿasā combines hope with intense fear and self-effacement.
rows.anchor: عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا مع التواضع لله في كلمة عسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham left the unbelievers and their land, God gave him prophetic children and the holy land; Isaac and Jacob consoled and strengthened him. Isaac was younger than Ishmael; Hagar's pregnancy provoked Sarah's jealousy before Sarah conceived Isaac.
rows.anchor: ولما فارق الكفار وأرضهم أبدله منهم أولادا أنبياء، والأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies God's mercy here with prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: هي النبوة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the mercy as wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: المال والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy is best understood broadly as religious and worldly good: knowledge, worldly rank and honor, and the bliss of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والأحسن أن يكون الخير الديني والدنيوي من العلم والمنزلة والشرف في الدنيا والنعيم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains a truthful, enduring tongue as lasting good praise of Abraham and his descendants.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression uses tongue for what the hand gives, and Arabic can use lisān for a message, whether good or bad, or for a people's language and speech.
rows.anchor: وعبر باللسان كما عبر باليد عما يطلق باليد وهي العطية. واللسان في كلام العرب الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Abraham's prayer by making him a model honored and invoked by all religious communities and by raising his descendants' remembrance; the passage links this to the command to follow Abraham's religion.
rows.anchor: استجاب الله دعوته واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين فصيره قدوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Juthū means to sit on one's knees, the posture of a frightened, humbled person; the verb has several attested forms.
rows.anchor: جثا: قعد على ركبتيه، وهي قعدة الخائف الذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥatama al-amr means to make an affair obligatory.
rows.anchor: حتم الأمر: أوجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nadī and al-nādī mean a gathering place for an event or consultation; it can also be the generous people's assembly or simply a meeting with people present. A line by Ḥātim illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: الندي والنادي: المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه لحادثة أو مشورة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī treats al-rayy as the verbal noun of being watered and also as a passive participle meaning watered.
rows.anchor: الري: مصدر رويت من الماء، واسم مفعول أي مروي قاله أبو علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-zī means collected beauties and derives from gathering.
rows.anchor: الزي: محاسن مجموعة من الزي وهو الجمع

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه والأخفش والمبرد وعامة البصريين
rows.claim: They take kallā as a particle of rebuke and deterrence.
rows.anchor: حرف ردع وزجر عند الخليل وسيبويه والأخفش والمبرد وعامة البصريين

rows.speaker: الكسائي ونصر بن يوسف وابن واصل وابن الأنباري
rows.claim: They interpret kallā as meaning 'indeed'.
rows.anchor: وذهب الكسائي ونصر بن يوسف وابن واصل وابن الأنباري إلى أنها بمعنى حقا

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Naḍr b. Shumayl takes kallā as an affirmative particle meaning 'yes'; it can also occur with an oath.
rows.anchor: إلى أنها حرف تصديق بمعنى نعم، وقد تستعمل مع القسم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن محمد الباهلي
rows.claim: He says kallā rejects what precedes it, may be a pause, and can elsewhere serve as a connective comparable to ayy.
rows.anchor: أن كلا رد لما قبلها فيجوز الوقف عليها وما بعدها استئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍidd can mean an ally: the ally is so named because he opposes one's enemy and helps against him.
rows.anchor: الضد: العون يقال: من أضدادكم أي أعوانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-azzu, al-hazzu, and al-istifzāz are related words for provoking and violently disturbing someone; the boiling, moving sound of a cauldron is called azīz.
rows.anchor: الأز والهز والاستفزاز أخوات، ومعناها التهييج وشدة الإزعاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafd means to arrive as an honored visitor.
rows.anchor: وفد يفد وفدا ووفودا ووفادة: قدم على سبيل التكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-add or al-idd means something astonishing, a grave outrage, or hardship; the related verb conveys that something weighed heavily on a person.
rows.anchor: الأد والإد: بفتح الهمزة وكسرها العجب. وقيل: العظيم المنكر والإدة الشدة

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawharī explains hadda as breaking or collapsing a building.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري هدا البناء هدا كسره

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says al-hadd is a fall with a loud sound, like a wall crashing down.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: هو سقوط بصوت شديد، والهدة صوت وقع الحائط ونحوه

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines al-hadd as forceful demolition.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: الهد الهدم الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rakz is a faint sound; the word also describes planting a spear's end in the ground and buried treasure. It can mean a subtle sound made without articulated speech or a mouth; a poetic line witnesses its use.
rows.anchor: الركز: الصوت الخفي، ومنه ركز الرمح غيب طرفه في الأرض

rows.speaker: أبو رزين ويحيى وقتادة والكوفيون
rows.claim: They read mukhlaṣan with fatḥa, meaning God singled Moses out for worship and prophethood, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: قرأ الكوفيون مخلصا بفتح اللام وهي قراءة أبي رزين ويحيى وقتادة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read mukhliṣan with kasra: Moses purified his worship of association and ostentation, or devoted himself to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة والجمهور بكسر اللام أي أخلص العبادة عن الشرك والرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's calling Moses means that God spoke to him; al-ṭūr is the well-known mountain in Syria.
rows.anchor: ونداؤه إياه هو تكليمه تعالى إياه. والطور الجبل المشهور بالشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ayman describes the mountain's side that was to Moses' right according to his position; it may instead mean a blessed side, but describing the side accords with the parallel verse.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأيمن صفة للجانب لقوله في آية أخرى جانب الطور الأيمن

rows.speaker: ابن القشيري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qushayrī supplies an omitted narrative: God called Moses as he returned from Midian, saw the fire in a tree, and sought someone to guide him to Egypt.
rows.anchor: قال ابن القشيري: في الكلام حذف وتقديره وناديناه حين أقبل من مدين ورأى النار

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand Moses' nearness as honor, privileged speech, and closeness to God.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور: تقريب التشريف والكلام واليوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية وميسرة
rows.claim: They say Moses was brought near to the unseen realm and the veils were lifted so that he heard the pens' scratching.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أدنى موسى من الملكوت ورفعت له الحجب حتى سمع صريف الأقلام

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Saʿīd says Gabriel carried Moses behind him.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد: أردفه جبريل على السلام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī likens the scene to a great person's bringing someone near for private conversation, while God spoke without an angelic intermediary.
rows.anchor: شبهه بمن قربه بعض العظماء للمناجاة حيث كلمه بغير واسطة ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najiyyan is an active participle meaning one engaged in private conversation, like jalīs; the word denotes confidential speech.
rows.anchor: ونجي فعيل من المناجاة بمعنى مناج كالجليس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets najāhu as 'he was truthful to him.'
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: معنى نجاه صدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in 'from Our mercy' can express the reason for the gift or partitive meaning, a portion of God's mercy.
rows.anchor: ومن في من رحمتنا للسبب أي من أجل رحمتنا له أو للتبعيض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses 'his brother' as an apposition to 'from Our mercy' and Hārūn as explanatory apposition.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وأخاه على هذا الوجه بدل وهارون عطف بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that parsing: 'his brother' is the direct object of 'We bestowed,' and need not be substituted for 'from Our mercy.' Hārūn was older; Moses asked for his support and prophethood, and God granted it.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن أخاه مفعول بقوله ووهبنا ولا ترادف من بعضا فتبدل منها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify this Ishmael as Abraham's son and the ancestor of both Arab lineages, Yemeni and Muḍarī.
rows.anchor: وإسماعيل هو ابن إبراهيم أبو العرب يمنيها ومضريها وهو قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies Ishmael as the son of Ḥizqīl, sent to his people, who injured his scalp; God offered punishment, but he chose pardon and God's reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه إسماعيل بن حزقيل، بعثه الله إلى قومه فشجوا جلدة رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was singled out for keeping promises because he fulfilled all promises to God and people, making this a famous, distinguishing quality.
rows.anchor: فوفى بالجميع، فلذلك خص بصدق الوعد

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Ishmael never made God a promise without fulfilling it, including patiently submitting to sacrifice.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: لم يعد ربه موعدة إلا أنجزها

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj also reports Ishmael promised a man to wait for him; the man returned after a year or twelve days and found him there.
rows.anchor: ووعد رجلا أن يقيم له بمكان فغاب عنه مدة. قيل: سنة. وقيل: اثنى عشر يوما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan understands Ishmael's household as his people and community; ʿAbd Allāh's codex reads 'his people.'
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: قومه وأمته، وفي مصحف عبد الله وكان يأمر قومه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says a prophet should begin by reforming and worshipping with his family, who are especially entitled to religious care; he cites commands to warn near kin, command family prayer, and protect one's household from fire.
rows.anchor: كان يبدأ بأهله في الأمر بالصلاح والعبادة ليجعلهم قدوة لمن وراءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes his household to be the entire community, since prophetic communities count as their families; the lesson is to advise outsiders and relatives, sharing religious benefits without neglect.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أهله أمته كلهم من القرابة وغيرهم، لأن أمم النبيين في عداد أهاليهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says Ishmael's truthful promise is mentioned as an honor, like the epithets 'forbearing,' 'devout,' and 'truthful,' and because it was his best-known trait.
rows.anchor: ذكر إسماعيل عليه السلام بصدق الوعد وإن كان موجودا في غيره من الأنبياء تشريفا له وإكراما

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read marḍiyyan, the passive participle 'approved'; its wāw changes to yāʾ because the ending follows a silent wāw, and this vowel change is preferable to retaining wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور مرضيا وهو اسم مفعول أي مرضو

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads marḍuwan with the wāw retained.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: مرضوا مصححا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idrīs is identified as Noah's grandfather, Akhnūkh; traditions credit him with astronomy, arithmetic, writing, sewing, clothing, prophethood, weights, measures, and weapons.
rows.anchor: هو جد أبي نوح وهو أخنوخ، وهو أول من نظر في النجوم والحساب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies Idrīs with Ilyās, sent to call his people to worship God and act freely; they refused and were destroyed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: هو إلياس بعث إلى قومه بأن يقولوا لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idrīs is a foreign proper name and so is diptote; it cannot be derived from Arabic dars, since with only properness as a diptote cause it would decline fully.
rows.anchor: وإدريس اسم أعجمي منع من الصرف للعلمية والعجمة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows that the name may have a similar meaning in its foreign language, which led someone to imagine an Arabic derivation; he says the elevated place means prophetic honor and nearness, and reports thirty revealed scrolls.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى إدريس في تلك اللغة قريبا من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elevated place may mean prophetic rank, honor, and standing with God, as for other prophets; another view takes it as physical ascent to heaven.
rows.anchor: المكان العلي شرف النبوة والزلفى عند الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God physically raised Idrīs, as He raised Jesus: an angel carried him to the fourth heaven, where the Angel of Death took his soul as foretold.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان ذلك بأمر الله كما رفع عيسى كان له خليل من الملائكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās places the event in the sixth heaven; some Miʿrāj reports from Abū Hurayra and Anas place Idrīs in the fourth.
rows.anchor: وروي أن هذا كله كان في السماء السادسة قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Idrīs was raised to Paradise, the highest place.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن: إلى الجنة لا شيء أعلى من الجنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Idrīs worships with angels in the seventh heaven and is also raised in Paradise as he wishes.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعبد الله مع الملائكة في السماء السابعة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says Idrīs is dead in heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هو ميت في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those points to the prophets previously mentioned; 'of the prophets' explains the group, while the second 'from' is partitive. Idrīs descends from Adam, Abraham from Noah's descendants, and Isaac, Ishmael, Jacob, and Israel from Abraham; Zechariah, John, Moses, Aaron, and Jesus descend from Israel through Mary.
rows.anchor: أولئك إشارة إلى من تقدم ذكره في هذه السورة من الأنبياء ومن في من النبيين للبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'And among those We guided' may attach to either preceding 'from'; 'those' is apparently the predicate, though it could modify 'those' with the conditional sentence as predicate.
rows.anchor: وممن هدينا يحتمل العطف على من الأولى أو الثانية

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verb 'are recited' with feminine tāʾ; several named readers use masculine yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تتلى بتاء التأنيث. وقرأ عبد الله وأبو جعفر وشيبة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls 'prostrating' an anticipated circumstantial state, since they are not prostrate at the instant they fall.
rows.anchor: وانتصب سجدا على الحال المقدرة قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukiyyan is the plural of bākin ('weeper'); the expected broken plural pattern is not attested though regular analogy would allow it.
rows.anchor: والبكي جمع باك كشاهد وشهود

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read bukiyyan with ḍamma on bāʾ; ʿAbd Allāh, Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read it with kasra, by vowel harmony with kāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بكيا بضم الباء وعبد الله ويحيى والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي بكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes bukiyyan as a plural matching the prior plural; it could instead be a verbal noun meaning weeping.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه جمع لمناسبة الجمع قبله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya insists the kasra reading is a verbal noun and can only be that.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وبكيا بكسر الباء وهو مصدر لا يحتمل غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's certainty: vowel harmony does not establish a verbal noun, as the plural juthiyyan is also read with kasra and ʿuṣiyy is similarly harmonized.
rows.anchor: وقوله ليس بسديد لأن إتباع حركة الكاف لا تعين المصدرية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say the heedless successors were Jews.
rows.anchor: نزل فخلف في اليهود عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says they included Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: وفيهم وفي النصارى عن السدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وعطاء ومحمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: They identify people in the Muslim community who, when its righteous members disappear, openly commit fornication in the alleys.
rows.anchor: في قوم من أمة الرسول يأتون عند ذهاب صالحيها يتبارزون بالزنا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the successors are coffee drinkers.
rows.anchor: وعن وهب: هم شرابو القهوة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والنخعي والقاسم بن مخيمرة ومجاهد وإبراهيم وعمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: They explain neglecting prayer as delaying it beyond its appointed time.
rows.anchor: إضاعة الصلاة تأخيرها عن وقتها قاله ابن مسعود والنخعي والقاسم بن مخيمرة

rows.speaker: القرظي والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Quraẓī, a view chosen by al-Zajjāj, defines neglect as failing to fulfill prayer's conditions.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي واختاره الزجاج: إضاعتها الإخلال بشروطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say they pray outside congregations, deny prayer's obligation, or close mosques and occupy themselves with crafts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إقامتها في غير الجماعات. وقيل: عدم اعتقاد وجوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desires here include anything desired that distracts from prayer and remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: والشهوات عام في كل مشتهى يشغل عن الصلاة وذكر الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī describes the worldly indulgence as building imposing structures, riding showy mounts, and wearing conspicuous clothes.
rows.anchor: وعن علي من بنى الشديد وركب المنظور ولبس المشهور

rows.speaker: عبد الله والحسن وأبو رزين العقيلي والضحاك وابن مقسم
rows.claim: They read ṣalawāt in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والحسن وأبو رزين العقيلي والضحاك وابن مقسم الصلوات جمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, ghayy can mean every kind of evil, with rushd denoting every kind of good; a cited line illustrates the contrast.
rows.anchor: والغي عند العرب كل شر، والرشاد كل خير

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj supplies an omitted noun: they will meet the recompense of error, as in the verse that mentions meeting athām.
rows.anchor: هو على حذف مضاف أي جزاء غي كقوله يلق أثاما

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets ghayy as loss and falling into perilous situations.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الغي الخسران والحصول في الورطات

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وعبد الله بن مسعود وكعب
rows.claim: They say Ghayy is a valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو وابن مسعود وكعب: غي واد في جهنم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd also gives the meaning 'misguidance.'
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: ضلال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says it may mean being led away from the path to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو غيا عن طريق الجنة

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī describes pits in Hell into which pus and blood flow.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكرماني: آبار في جهنم يسيل إليها الصديد والقيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says ghayy is destruction.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكرماني: آبار في جهنم يسيل إليها الصديد والقيح. وقيل: هلاك

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash reports a reading yulqawna with passive-like vowel pattern and a doubled qāf.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فيما حكى الأخفش يلقون بضم الياء وفتح اللام وشد القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception 'except whoever repents' is apparently connected to those threatened with Ghayy.
rows.anchor: إلا من تاب استثناء ظاهره الاتصال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats the exception as disconnected; the following 'believed' suggests neglecting prayer had been unbelief.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: منقطع وآمن هذا يدل على أن تلك الإضاعة كفر

rows.speaker: الحسن والزهري وحميد وشيبة والأعمش وابن أبي ليلى وابن مناذر وابن سعدان
rows.claim: They read yadkhulūn actively, as do these readers at every other Qur'anic occurrence of the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن يدخلون مبنيا للفاعل، وكذا كل ما في القرآن من يدخلون

rows.speaker: ابن غزوان عن طلحة
rows.claim: Ibn Ghazwān from Ṭalḥa reads sayadkhulūn, with active voice and the future sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن غزوان عن طلحة: سيدخلون بسين الاستقبال مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read jannāt in the accusative as a plural apposition to al-janna; the clause 'they will not be wronged' is parenthetical or circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور جنات نصبا جمعا بدلا من الجنة

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو حيوة وعيسى بن عمر والأعمش وأحمد بن موسى عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: These readers put jannāt in the nominative plural, understood as 'those are gardens'; al-Zamakhsharī analyzes it as a subject with 'which' as predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو حيوة وعيسى بن عمر والأعمش وأحمد بن موسى عن أبي عمرو جنات رفعا جمعا

rows.speaker: الحسن بن حي وعلي بن صالح
rows.claim: They read jannata ʿadn in the accusative singular, a reading also reported from al-Aʿmash and found in ʿAbd Allāh's codex.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن حي وعلي بن صالح جنة عدن نصبا مفردا

rows.speaker: اليماني والحسن وإسحاق الأزرق عن حمزة
rows.claim: They read jannatu ʿadn in the nominative singular; if ʿAdn is a proper name, allatī is an adjective, while if it means abiding, it is an apposition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليماني والحسن وإسحاق الأزرق عن حمزة جنة رفعا مفردا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls ʿAdn a proper name for abiding or for Paradise as a place of residence, to explain the syntax and description.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: عدن معرفة علم لمعنى العدن وهو الإقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says neither proposed proper-name sense is established by Arabic evidence; Basran grammarians allow an indefinite apposition to a definite noun, and allatī need not be an adjective, so al-Zamakhsharī's constraints fail.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره متعقب. أما دعواه أن عدنا علم لمعنى العدن فيحتاج إلى توقيف وسماع من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayb can mean that Paradise is unseen by them, that they are absent from it, or belief in the unseen as the reason for the promise; Abū Muslim instead takes them as worshippers of God in secret.
rows.anchor: وبالغيب حال أي وعدها وهي غائبة عنهم أو وهم غائبون عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent antecedent of His promise is the verbal noun; maʾtiyyan may mean 'coming' or retain passive sense, 'attained.' Al-Zamakhsharī prefers the first sense because the promised Garden is approached by its people, echoing Ibn Jurayj.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن وعده مصدر. فقيل: مأتيا بمعنى آتيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Except salām' is a disconnected exception and may be the angels' greeting to the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: إلا سلاما استثناء منقطع وهو قول الملائكة سلام عليكم بما صبرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God greets them as they enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يسلم الله عليهم عند دخولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening describe receiving food twice during a day-night period.
rows.anchor: ومعنى بكرة وعشيا يأتيهم طعامهم مرتين في مقدار اليوم والليلة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says there is no actual morning or evening in Paradise; its people receive what they desire, as they did in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لا بكرة ولا عشي ولكن يؤتون به على ما كانوا يشتهون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda similarly says the wording addresses them through familiar Arab expressions for comfortable living.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر نحوه قتادة أن تكون مخاطبة بما تعرف العرب في رفاهة العيش

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the phrasing invokes Arabs' idea of luxury: many had only one meal a day and lived on wild plants and animals.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: خوطبوا على ما كانت العرب تعلم من أفضل العيش

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines laghw as useless, surplus talk and sees the verse as a lesson to shun idle speech, which God excludes even from a place without religious duties.
rows.anchor: اللغو فضول الكلام وما لا طائل تحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the greeting were mere idle speech, it is the sole exception, as in the cited verse about passing by idle talk with dignity; the cited line about swords' only flaw provides a rhetorical analogy.
rows.anchor: وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is disconnected: their speech is free of fault. A greeting appears unnecessary because they are already safe, but it still benefits them through its content.
rows.anchor: أو لا يسمعون فيها إلا قولا يسلمون فيه من العيب والنقيصة على الاستثناء المنقطع

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says Paradise has no literal night or day; the terms are approximate because Arabs associate two meals with luxury, or they indicate continuous provision.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون ثم ليل ولا نهار ولكن على التقدير

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read nūrith as the present tense of awratha; al-Aʿmash makes the pronoun referring to the relative explicit, while several readers have a doubled rāʾ and fatḥa on wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور نورث مضارع أورث، والأعمش نورثها بإبراز الضمير العائد على الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance is a metaphor: the God-fearing finish their deeds, while the fruit of those deeds, Paradise, remains for them like inherited property. Another view says they inherit the dwellings of Hell's inhabitants had they obeyed.
rows.anchor: والتوريث استعارة أي تبقى عليه الجنة كما يبقى على الوارث مال الموروث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel once delayed visiting the Prophet; when he came, the Prophet said he missed him and asked whether he might visit more often, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أبطأ جبريل عن الرسول مرة، فلما جاء قال: «يا جبريل قد اشتقت إليك

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk connect the revelation to Gabriel's delay in answering the questions discussed in Sūrat al-Kahf, comparing it with al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك: سببها أن جبريل عليه السلام تأخر في السؤالات المتقدمة في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanazzul may express gradual, repeated action after nuzzaltuhu, or simply mean nazala without a sense of gradual continuation; a poetic line illustrates ordinary descent.
rows.anchor: وتنزل تفعل وهي للمطاوعة وهي أحد معاني تفعل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives tanazzul two senses, descent gradually or descent generally, and takes gradual descent as appropriate here, describing visits spaced over time.
rows.anchor: التنزل على معنيين: معنى النزول على مهل، ومعنى النزول على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the wāw links one sentence to another without requiring the two statements to have identical meanings.
rows.anchor: وهذه الواو التي في قوله وما نتنزل هي عاطفة جملة كلام على أخرى

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh attributes to some a weak view that the verse continues Gabriel's words to Mary, beginning 'I am only your Lord's messenger.'
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش عن قوم أن قوله وما نتنزل متصل بقوله إنما أنا رسول ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse closes the stories of favored prophets and their descendants, then addresses Muḥammad, himself descended from Abraham; the negligent successors were scriptural communities whose behavior caused Quraysh and Jews to question the Prophet, and the delay pleased them. Gabriel explains that revelation's timing belongs to God, absolving himself; the verse states the result rather than the worldly desire and hidden malice that caused it.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر في مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها أنه تعالى لما ذكر قصة زكريا ومريم وذكر إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya takes 'before us' as the world up to the first blast, 'behind us' as the afterlife from resurrection, and 'between' as the interval between the two blasts.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: ما بين الأيدي الدنيا بأسرها إلى النفخة الأولى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Abū al-ʿĀliya's explanation fits human beings, whereas the speech belongs to angels.
rows.anchor: وقول أبي العالية إنما يتصور في بني آدم، وهذه المقالة هي للملائكة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says what is before them is time before creation, behind them is after death through the eternal afterlife, and between is lifetime.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: ما بين الأيدي هو ما مر من الزمان قبل الإيجاد

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس وابن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل وسفيان
rows.claim: They reverse the spatial labels: before is the afterlife, behind is this world, with the interval between them in between.
rows.anchor: ما بين أيدينا الآخرة وما خلفنا الدنيا رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid gives the opposite mapping from the preceding report.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عكسه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash takes before as before creation, behind as after annihilation, and between as the span from this world to the next; elsewhere he says 'between' means their present state.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ما بين أيدينا قبل أن نخلق وما خلفنا بعد الفناء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة وأبو العالية
rows.claim: They also identify 'between' as the time between the two trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة وأبو العالية: ما بين النفختين

rows.speaker: صاحب الغينان
rows.claim: The author of al-Ghīnān says before is the angels' descent from heaven, behind is the earth, and between is the space from heaven to earth.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الغينان: ما بين أيدينا نزول الملائكة من السماء

rows.speaker: ابن القشيري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qushayrī adopts Ibn Jurayj's view and summarizes the three times as all belonging to God, who creates and directs them and controls when revelation descends.
rows.anchor: حصر الأزمنة الثلاثة وهي أن كلها لله هو منشئها ومدبر أمرها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the point is God's ownership of the angels: all their movement and activity occurs by His wisdom and command; before, behind, and between may denote their locations and stations.
rows.anchor: إنما القصد الإشعار بملك الله تعالى لملائكته

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī likewise understands the words spatially: angels cannot move from one place or direction to another except by the King's command, for He encompasses everything.
rows.anchor: ما قدامنا وما خلفنا من الجهات والأماكن. وما نحن فيها

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī interprets 'to Him belongs' as meaning that He knows what is before them.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي: له علم ما بين أيدينا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم وابن بحر
rows.claim: Abū Muslim and Ibn Baḥr say 'We do not descend' is not the angels' speech but the people of Paradise speaking to each other; the verses describe entry into Paradise and what lies before, behind, and between the two lives.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم وابن بحر: وما نتنزل الآية ليس من كلام الملائكة وإنما هو من كلام أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also reports that the pious say they enter Paradise only with God's permission and reward; God owns past, present, and future and enables good deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي حكاية قول المتقين حين يدخلون الجنة أي وما ننزل الجنة إلا بإذن من الله علينا بثواب أعمالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not forgetful of workers or unaware of the reward due them; forgetfulness is impossible for the Lord of the heavens, earth, and all between them.
rows.anchor: وما كان ربك نسيا لأعمال العاملين غافلا عما يجب أن يثابوا به

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī rejects the paradise-speaker interpretation: the apparent descent is angels coming to the Prophet, the singular addressee does not suit a group speaking among themselves, and the following description of the Lord does not fit that scene.
rows.anchor: هذا مخالف للظاهر من وجوه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read tanazzalu with nūn, referring to Gabriel and the angels; al-Aʿraj reads yāʾ as a statement from God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وما نتنزل بالنون عنى جبريل نفسه والملائكة. وقرأ الأعرج بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the yāʾ verb refer to Gabriel; Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that the following words 'to Him belong what is before us' do not fit this smoothly.
rows.anchor: قيل: والضمير في يتنزل عائد على جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the better reading is a report from Gabriel that the Qur'an descends only when God sets its time; al-Zamakhsharī also treats it as Gabriel's speech, with the pronoun referring to revelation.
rows.anchor: وإنما يتجه أن يكون خبرا عن جبريل أن القرآن لا يتنزل إلا بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report can be understood as Gabriel saying that he descends only by God's command and that God controls the angels; he excuses the delay and assures Muḥammad that God has not forgotten him.
rows.anchor: ويحمل ذلك القول على إضمار أي وما يتنزل جبريل إلا بأمر ربك قائلا له ما بين أيدينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A revelation report says a Quraysh man, identified by some as Ubayy b. Khalaf, brought a decayed bone, blew on it, and mocked the Prophet by asking whether it would be resurrected.
rows.anchor: قيل: سبب النزول أن رجلا من قريش قيل هو أبي بن خلف جاء بعظم رفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic attribution may represent a group through what some members did, a generic unbeliever who denies resurrection, or a particular man; alternatives named are al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, Abū Jahl, and al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra. A line by al-Farazdaq shows such collective attribution.
rows.anchor: أو المعني أبي بن خلف، أو المعاصي بن وائل، أو أبو جهل، أو الوليد بن المغيرة أقوال

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read a-idha with the interrogative hamza; a group, including Ibn Dhakwān in one report, reads idha without it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور أإذا بهمزة الاستفهام. وقرأت فرقة منهم ابن ذكوان بخلاف عنه إذا بدون همزة الاستفهام

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read lasawfa; Ṭalḥa b. Muṣarrif reads sa-ukhraju without lām and with the future sīn, allowing idha to be governed by the verb despite the future particle; a poetic example is offered.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور لسوف باللام. وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف سأخرج بغير لام وسين الاستقبال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the lām of the initial clause emphasizes the future rather than making the verb present, analogizing the lām's emptied function to the hamza in Allāh.
rows.anchor: لم تجامعها إلا مخلصة للتوكيد كما أخلصت الهمزة في يا ألله للتعويض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that not all grammarians assign the lām a present sense and challenges al-Zamakhsharī's analogy: the hamza's origin and possible deletion in the vocative do not establish a compensatory function.
rows.anchor: وما ذكر من أن اللام تعطي معنى الحال مخالف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving resurrection, God swears by Himself in association with His Messenger to honor and exalt him; such oaths recur in the Qur'an to raise the Prophet's standing.
rows.anchor: ولما أقام تعالى الحجة الدامغة على حقية البعث أقسم على ذلك باسمه مضافا إلى رسوله تشريفا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw before the devils can coordinate them or mean 'with': each unbeliever is paired with the devil who misled him, in a chain, if the pronoun refers only to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والواو في والشياطين للعطف أو بمعنى مع يحشرون مع قرنائهم من الشياطين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية والزمخشري
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and initially al-Zamakhsharī take the pronoun in 'We shall surely gather them' as the unbelievers alone, followed by a report about them.
rows.anchor: وهذا إذا كان الضمير في لنحشرنهم للكفرة وهو قول ابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense includes all creation, believing and unbelieving; everyone is brought to Hell's edge so believers witness the terrors they escaped and rejoice at their enemies' fate.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه عام للخلق كلهم مؤمنهم وكافرهم ولم يفرق بين المؤمنين والكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun is general, all kneel at the arrival point by Hell as they had during judgment, before receiving reward or punishment, as in the description of every community kneeling.
rows.anchor: يتجاثون عند موافاة شاطىء جهنم كما كانوا في الموقف متجاثين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains jithiyyan as seated; he also gives the sense 'groups,' from jathwa, a heap of earth or stones.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: قعودا، وعنه جماعات جماعات جمع جثوة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن والزجاج
rows.claim: Mujāhid, al-Hasan, and al-Zajjāj say the people are on their knees.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن والزجاج: على الركب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says they are upright on their knees because the place is crowded.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي قياما على الركب لضيق المكان بهم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: They read jithiyyan, ʿitiyyan, and ṣilliyyan with kasra; the majority use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص جثيا وعتيا وصليا بكسر الجيم والعين والصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then We will extract may mean taking them out, as in the verse about Moses' hand, or casting them like an arrow from a bow; al-shīʿa means a group bound by a doctrine.
rows.anchor: ثم لننزعن أي لنخرجن كقوله ونزع يده

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ's line says the greatest offenders are taken first.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الأحوص: يبدأ بالأكابر فالأكابر جرما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the worst and most defiant are selected from each faction and cast into Hell in order of severity.
rows.anchor: يمتاز من كل طائفة من طوائف الغي والفساد أعصاهم فأعصاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ayyuhum refers to those gathered; the nominative reading has several grammatical analyses, and the dispute belongs to syntax.
rows.anchor: والضمير في أيهم عائد على المحشورين المحضرين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows extracting some from every group, with 'which of them' supplying the answer to an implied question.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون النزع واقعا على من كل شيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls this analysis an unnecessary ellipsis that turns one apparent sentence into two.
rows.anchor: وهذا تكلف وادعاء إضمار لا ضرورة تدعو إليه

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl relates the construction to a poetic line and analyzes ayyuhum as a quoted expression in the clause.
rows.anchor: وقرن الخليل تخريجه بقول الشاعر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers al-Khalīl's analysis; al-Naḥḥās reports that al-Zajjāj called Sībawayh mistaken.
rows.anchor: ورجح الزجاج قول الخليل وذكر عنه النحاس أنه غلط سيبويه في هذه المسألة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh argues that this does not entail allowing the same construction with a singular adjective; the verse is a sentence, on which the verb's scope is greater than over one noun.
rows.anchor: وليس بلازم من حيث هذه أسماء مفردة والآية جملة

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: They explain nanziʿanna as meaning 'we shall call out,' so the verb does not govern ayyuhum.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الكسائي أن معنى لننزعن لنناذين فعومل معاملته

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī says the vocative is syntactically nominative when followed by a clause and governs the meaning, not the surface form.
rows.anchor: ونادى تعلق إذا كان بعده جملة نصب فتعمل في المعنى ولا تعمل في اللفظ

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad attaches ayyuhum to shīʿa and understands the people of a faction as considering which member is most defiant; this requires an omitted object.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: أيهم متعلق بشيعة

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls al-Mubarrad's proposal a good analysis, with cooperation understood in the root of tashāyaʿū.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا قول حسن

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن شقير
rows.claim: Ibn Shuayr reports a Kūfan view that ayyuhum contains a conditional sense, meaning whether they are defiant or not.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو بكر بن شقير أن بعض الكوفيين يقول: في أيهم معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف ومعاذ بن مسلم وزائدة عن الأعمش
rows.claim: They read ayyahum in the accusative as the object of nanziʿanna; these readings support the possibility of inflection when the relative clause's head is omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف ومعاذ بن مسلم الهراء أستاذ الفراء وزائدة عن الأعمش أيهم بالنصب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الجرمي
rows.claim: Al-Jarmī says that between Basra and Mecca he heard no one pronounce the construction with nominative ayyuhum.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو الجرمي: خرجت من البصرة فلم أسمع منذ فارقت الخندق إلى مكة أحدا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās says the grammarians he knew faulted Sībawayh here and quotes al-Zajjāj saying only two errors in Sībawayh's book were apparent, this being one.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر النحاس: وما علمت أحدا من النحويين إلا وقد خطأ سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic idiom 'we came to the water' can mean entering or visiting a tribe's territory, not reaching its water itself.
rows.anchor: وتقول العرب: وردنا ماء بني تميم وبني كلب إذا حضروهم ودخلوا بلادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the address to be specifically to unbelievers, so their 'passing by' is entry into Hell; another view says believers and unbelievers enter it, though it does not harm believers, a claim the author declines to elaborate because he finds it repellent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخطاب للكفار أي قل لهم يا محمد فيكون الورود في حقهم الدخول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة
rows.claim: They read wa-in minhum with third-person hāʾ, matching the preceding pronouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة وإن منهم بالهاء للغيبة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the word may mean kneeling around Hell; if only unbelievers are meant, the sense is clear. He takes the implied subject of kāna as the act of arrival, decreed as inevitable.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالورود جثوهم حولها وإن أريد الكفار خاصة فالمعنى بين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read thumma as a conjunction, supporting a general sense of passage; ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ubayy, ʿAlī, and others read thamma ('there'), with Ibn Abī Laylā pausing with hāʾ of pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ثم بحرف العطف وهذا يدل على أن الورود عام

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read nunajjī with doubled jīm; Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Muḥayṣin use a still nūn and light jīm; another group reads with one nūn and doubled jīm; ʿAlī reads nunḥī with ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ننجي بفتح النون وتشديد الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ittaqaw is omitted and understood as idolatry; the ظلم here is unbelief.
rows.anchor: ومفعول اتقوا محذوف أي الشرك والظلم هنا ظلم الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about clear signs was revealed concerning al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith and his companions: poor Companions wore rough clothes while polytheists groomed their hair and wore fine silk and clothes.
rows.anchor: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات نزلت في النضر بن الحارث وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They asked which faction had the better home and gathering, assuming worldly comfort showed God's favor; the author links this taunt to the preceding proof about resurrection.
rows.anchor: فقالوا للمؤمنين: أي الفريقين خير مقاما أي منزلا وسكنا وأحسن نديا

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن
rows.claim: They read yutlā in masculine form; the majority read feminine tatlā, since believers recited the Qur'an to unbelievers and praised the Prophet's signs.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن يتلى بالياء والجمهور بالتاء من فوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers argued that God favors His beloved people, then pointed to their own wealth and fine appearance as proof they were better than the poor believers.
rows.anchor: إنما يحسن الله لأحب الخلق إليه وينعم على أهل الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyināt may mean carefully ordered wording and concise meaning, manifest miraculousness, or proofs; the adjective reinforces a quality always true of God's signs.
rows.anchor: ومعنى بينات مرتلات الألفاظ ملخصات المعاني أو ظاهرات الإعجاز أو حججا وبراهين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read maqāman with fatḥa; Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ḥamīd and others read it with ḍamma. Either vowel allows a verbal noun or a place of standing/residence, and the word is accusative of specification.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور مقاما بفتح الميم. وقرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed many generations who had better worldly circumstances to warn the taunting unbelievers that He can destroy them too, and to prompt reflection; fine possessions and refreshment did not save deniers.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى كثرة ما أهلك من القرون ممن كان أحسن حالا منهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: They parse 'they are better' as an adjective of kam, which requires placing the adjective in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وهم أحسن في محل النصب صفة لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says interrogative or exclamatory kam is neither modified nor a modifier in Basran grammar; hum ahsan instead modifies qarn, pluralized because a generation contains many individuals, though singular agreement would also be Arabic.
rows.anchor: ونص أصحابنا على أن كم الاستفهامية والخبرية لا توصف ولا يوصف بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation of athāth has already been discussed in Sūrat al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: وتقدم تفسير الأثاث في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read riʾyan with hamza, a form of vision meaning something seen, like grinding and watering as verbal nouns with passive force.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ورءيا بالهمزة من رؤية العين فعل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains al-riʾy as appearance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الرئي المنظر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets it as forms or figures.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه صورا

rows.speaker: الزهري وأبو جعفر وشيبة وطلحة وأيوب وابن سعدان وابن ذكوان وقالون
rows.claim: They read riyyan with a doubled yāʾ and no hamza; it may derive from hamzated rawāʾ ('appearance'), with hamza eased and the two yāʾs assimilated, or from rayy ('well-watered'), evoking freshness and beauty.
rows.anchor: بتشديد الياء من غير همز، فاحتمل أن يكون مهموز الأصل من الرواء والمنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mardā means a return or destination; the author notes that the remaining good deeds were already explained in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: ومردا معناه مرجعا وتقدم تفسير الباقيات الصالحات في الكهف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's first reading links the boast about worldly standing with the following 'until they see what is promised': the unbelievers repeat their taunt until worldly Muslim victory or Judgment reveals their worse standing and weaker forces.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية وجهان أحدهما أن تكون متصلة بالآية التي هي رابعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls that linkage extremely remote because a long span and two parenthetical sentences separate the boast from its proposed endpoint; Abū ʿAlī would not allow this.
rows.anchor: انتهى هذا الوجه وهو في غاية البعد لطول الفصل بين قوله قالوا: أي الفريقين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's second reading connects the phrase with what follows, contrasting their 'better station' and 'finer assembly' with the believers' rivals who are worse in place and weaker in forces; either promised punishment or the Hour is the object they see.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن يتصل بما يليها فذكر نحوا مما قدمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text turns from the deluded person's worldly boasting to the guided person's increase in guidance and enduring good deeds, which replace transient luxury.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر إمداد الضال في ضلالته وارتباكه في الافتخار بنعم الدنيا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī coordinates 'and God increases' with the position of 'let the Most Merciful extend,' making the deluded person increase in error by abandonment and the guided person increase in guidance through divine aid.
rows.anchor: يزيد معطوف على موضع فليمدد لأنه واقع موقع الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that coordination: the sentence 'God increases those guided in guidance' has no pronoun linking it to the antecedent, as a coordinated predicate or conditional consequence requires.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون ويزيد معطوفا على موضع فليمدد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains 'better reward' and 'better return' as better than unbelievers' boasts, with return meaning outcome or benefit.
rows.anchor: هي خير ثوابا من مفاخرات الكفار وخير مردا أي وخير مرجعا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Asked how believers' reward can be compared with unbelievers' nonexistent reward, al-Zamakhsharī says their reward is Hell, using ironic mockery more galling than a direct threat; everyday comparisons such as summer being hotter than winter mean greater intensity.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل ثوابهم النار على طريقة قوله فأعتبوا بالصيلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two poetic lines illustrate the ironic calling of a punishment or harmful outcome a greeting or reward, supporting al-Zamakhsharī's interpretation of rhetorical mockery.
rows.anchor: تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, who owed Khabbāb b. al-Aratt for work; he demanded that Khabbāb disbelieve in Muḥammad before he would pay. Khabbāb refused, saying God would raise him after death, and al-ʿĀṣ boasted he would then have wealth and children to pay.
rows.anchor: نزلت في العاصي بن وائل عمل له خباب بن الأرت عملا وكان قينا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse concerns al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, who made similar claims.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because seeing can lead to full knowledge and reliable reporting, araʾayta is used idiomatically to mean 'tell'; the fāʾ marks a succeeding story, and the signs are the Qur'an and proofs of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت رؤية الأشياء سبيلا إلى الإحاطة بها وصحة الخبر عنها استعملوا أرأيت بمعنى أخبر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read waladan with fatḥa in all four occurrences here and in al-Zukhruf; the word denotes the generic category rather than a single child.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ولدا أربعتهن هنا، وفي الزخرف بفتح اللام والواو

rows.speaker: الأعمش وطلحة والكسائي وابن أبي ليلى وابن عيسى الأصبهاني
rows.claim: They read wuld with ḍamma on wāw and sukūn on lām; some take it as a broken plural of walad, supported by poetry, and others as synonymous with walad, supported by another poetic line.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة والكسائي وابن أبي ليلى وابن عيسى الأصبهاني بضم الواو وإسكان اللام

rows.speaker: عبد الله ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They read wulid with kasra on wāw and still lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ويحيى بن يعمر بكسر الواو وسكون اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza in aṭṭalaʿa is interrogative and is balanced by am; a reading drops it when linking speech, as in a poetic example that implies 'did he reach?'
rows.anchor: والهمزة في أطلع للاستفهام، ولذلك عادلتها أم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Araʾayta follows Sībawayh's pattern: it takes one direct object and a question as its second object; other constructions of araʾayta meaning 'tell me' can be reconciled with this analysis.
rows.anchor: وجاء التركيب في أرأيت على الوضع الذي ذكره سيبويه من أنها تتعدى لواحد تنصبه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains aṭṭalaʿa al-ghayb as climbing to a mountain's summit, or rising over a mountain pass; Jarīr's line uses the word for mountain ascent.
rows.anchor: أطلع الغيب من قولهم: أطلع الجبل إذا ارتقى إلى أعلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diction emphasizes the enormity of his claim: could he have ascended to the unique knowledge of the unseen? He could only expect the promised gift through unseen knowledge or a covenant from its Knower.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن ما ادعى أن يؤتاه وتألى عليه لا يتوصل إليه إلا بأحد هذين الطريقين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the covenant as a righteous deed already performed, on which the man bases his expectation.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هل له عمل صالح قدمه فهو يرجو بذلك ما يقول

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī asks whether God had promised him that He would grant him those things.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي: هل عهد الله إليه أن يؤتيه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes him and alerts him that his assumption and wish are mistaken; writing his boast stands for the punishment that follows, hence the future sīn in 'We shall write.'
rows.anchor: وكلا ردع وتنبيه على الخطأ الذي هو مخطئ فيما تصوره لنفسه

rows.speaker: أبو نهيك
rows.claim: Abū Nuhayk reads kallā with tanwīn twice, treating it as the verbal noun kalla, 'the sword failed to strike,' and supplies an implied verb: be weakened from worship or truth.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو نهيك كلا بالتنوين فيهما هنا وهو مصدر من كل السيف كلا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives two senses of 'We shall write': his statement will become manifest and be shown to have been recorded, or the phrase is a conventional threat promising eventual revenge despite delay.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فيه وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future promise 'We shall extend for him' means prolonging his torment or increasing and multiplying its duration.
rows.anchor: ونمد أي نطول له من العذاب الذي يعذب به المستهزءون أو نزيده من العذاب

rows.speaker: الجمهور والأعمش
rows.claim: The majority read sanaktubu with nūn; al-Aʿmash reads it with passive voice, yāʾ and tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور سنكتب بالنون والأعمش بياء مضمومة والتاء مفتوحة مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib reads wa-namuddu lahu with an explicit plural verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب ونمد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To inherit what he says means stripping him of wealth and children so God receives them as heir; the verb says in the present while its meaning is past: what he said.
rows.anchor: ونرثه ما يقول أي نسلبه المال والولد فنكون كالوارث له

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says God will make the Paradise the man wishes for belong to someone else.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: نجعل ما يتمنى من الجنة لغيره

rows.speaker: أبو سهيل
rows.claim: Abū Suhayl says God deprives him of the wealth and children he wishes for and assigns them to another.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سهيل: نحرمه ما يتمناه من المال والولد ونجعله لغيره

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests the boast concerns hoped-for worldly wealth and children: even if granted, they will be taken away, and he will come alone after death, as in the verse 'You have come to Us singly.' Alternatively, death ends his boasting.
rows.anchor: هب أنا أعطيناه ما اشتهاه إما نرثه منه في العاقبة ويأتينا فردا غدا

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says God preserves the man's words against him for the final outcome, as scholars are called heirs of the prophets because they preserve their words.
rows.anchor: ونرثه ما يقول معناه نحفظه عليه للعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fardan conveys humiliation and lack of supporters.
rows.anchor: وفردا تتضمن ذلته وعدم أنصاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in 'they took' refer to worshipped idols; the later plural pronouns return to the wrongdoers in the prior verse. The purpose lām says they hoped the idols would be a source of strength, rescue, and benefit.
rows.anchor: والضمير في واتخذوا لعبادة الأصنام وقد تقدم ما يعود عليه وهم الظالمون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes kallā as rebuking and denying the idolaters' claim that idols strengthen them.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: كلا ردع لهم وإنكار لتعززهم بالآلهة

rows.speaker: أبو نهيك
rows.claim: Abū Nuhayk is reported to read kallā yakfurūna bi-ʿibādatihim; Ibn Jinnī records kallan with fatḥa and tanwīn, which he explains as 'all this opinion and belief.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن نهيك كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the tanwīn, if genuine, belongs to the usual rebuke particle, not a new word; its alif does not become nūn, and the comparison to qawārīrā is unsound because that noun's tanwīn reflects declension or dialect.
rows.anchor: فليس بجيد لأنه قال إنها التي للردع، والتي للردع حرف ولا وجه لقلب ألفها نونا

rows.speaker: أبو نهيك
rows.claim: Other authorities transmit Abū Nuhayk reading kallā with fatḥa and tanwīn as an adjective of the idols, or with ḍamma and tanwīn as an omitted verb's object meaning they reject or leave them; al-Ṭabarī reports kullu with nominative as a subject.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وهو يعني كلا نعت للآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent antecedent of 'they will deny' is the idols, the nearest topic: the idols will disown their worship, as in the cited verses. The alternative is that the polytheists deny their association after disaster, but 'they will become opponents' favors keeping the pronouns on one referent.
rows.anchor: فالأظهر أن الضمير في سيكفرون عائد على أقرب مذكور محدث عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delayed reckoning may be when God's promise occurs; 'they will deny their worship' or 'become their opponents' may clarify its content, or 'counting' itself may imply requital. Alternatively, on the Day of Gathering God will do to both groups what cannot be described; the final parse of yawm is best.
rows.anchor: متى يكون ذلك أو سيكفرون بعبادتهم أو بيكونون عليهم ضدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious are gathered 'to the Merciful' to honor them; the name conveys that they go to one who will show them mercy despite the coercive sense of gathering over long distances.
rows.anchor: وعدي نحشر بإلى الرحمن تعظيما لهم وتشريفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Driving the sinners to Hell conveys distress and shame, while calling the pious a الوفد evokes honored envoys awaiting a king's generosity.
rows.anchor: ولفظ السوق فيه إزعاج وهو إن عدي بإلى جهنم تفظيعا لهم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says the pious ride camels whose howdahs are gold and whose mounts have ruby saddles; he also describes jeweled camels with ruby and emerald reins.
rows.anchor: وعن علي: على نوق رحالها ذهب، وعلى نجائب سرجها ياقوت

rows.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الملائي
rows.claim: ʿAmr b. Qays al-Mullāʾī says they ride beautiful images of their righteous deeds; another report says each rides what he prefers, including elephant, horse, or ship that carries them afloat.
rows.anchor: وروى عمرو بن قيس الملائي أنهم يركبون على تماثيل من أعمالهم الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This honored arrival follows the reckoning and is the journey to Paradise. They are compared to royal envoys as the noblest and finest looking people, though it is not a literal delegation because they remain forever in their Lord's reward.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الوفادة بعد انقضاء الحساب وأنها النهوض إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والحسن
rows.claim: They interpret al-wird as the thirsty, named for the cause because whoever approaches water does so from thirst; lexically, wird is the verbal noun of heading to water.
rows.anchor: والورد العطاش قاله ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن والجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Jaḥdarī read yuḥsharu al-muttaqūn and yusāqu al-mujrimūn in passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والجحدري يحشر المتقون ويساق المجرمون مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'they do not possess' may refer to all creation, the two groups just mentioned; the exception can be connected to it, or a following statement. If it refers only to the guilty, it means they cannot intercede and the exception is disconnected.
rows.anchor: والضمير في لا يملكون عائد على الخلق الدال عليهم ذكر المتقين والمجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronoun in 'they do not possess' to refer to both the pious and guilty; a further view limits it to the pious. Taking a covenant means performing the good deed that earns a place among those who intercede.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عائد على المتقين، واتخاذ العهد هو العمل الصالح الذي يحصل به في حيز من يشفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports abound that learned and righteous people intercede; a hadith says one person from the Prophet's community will intercede for more than Banū Tamīm, and Qatāda says martyrs intercede for seventy.
rows.anchor: وتظافرت الأحاديث على أن أهل العلم والصلاح يشفعون فيشفعون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the martyr intercedes for seventy people.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: كنا نحدث أن الشهيد يشفع في سبعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun means the pious, the exception may identify only those for whom intercession is granted; on the other reading it identifies the intercessors. The author explains the syntax with an omitted 'intercession' and cites poetry.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون من اتخذ المشفوع فيهم، وعلى التأويل الأول يكون من اتخذ الشافعين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the plural wāw could be a plural marker rather than a pronoun, with the singular 'whoever takes' as the understood agent.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن تكون يعني الواو في لا يملكون علامة للجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects resorting to this rare dialect when the wāw is plainly a pronoun; Ibn ʿUṣfūr calls the language weak, and plural markers are not attested with a singular-looking agent without transmitted evidence.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي حمل القرآن على هذه اللغة القليلة مع وضوح جعل الواو ضميرا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows taking min as an accusative through an omitted genitive: 'except the intercession of one who has taken a covenant.'
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب يعني من على تقدير حذف المضاف أي إلا شفاعة من اتخذ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the covenant is the testimony that there is no god but God and Muḥammad is God's Messenger.
rows.anchor: والعهد هنا. قال ابن عباس: لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله
